properties.statement: AN AGENT WORKING THIS TOOL PROPOSED A PLAN BEFORE ASKING THE GRAPH WHAT IT ALREADY KNEW — THREE TIMES IN ONE SESSION. Recorded because each instance was caught by a different mechanism and only the pattern shows the failure is systematic rather than three accidents. || (1) SETTING `medium: REST` ON `ifc:mcp-tools-http` to close an incomplete-contract gap, when THAT NODE'S OWN `spec` FIELD argues at length that `unspecified` is the honest answer and that REST is positively wrong. Caught by reading the node one step too late; reverted within the minute. (2) PROPOSING CONTRACTS FOR 64 ‘UNCONTRACTED’ MODULE PAIRS, and getting them approved, when `fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet` — recorded TWO DAYS EARLIER — said all 64 sit inside one crate, that most are impl blocks of one struct, and that the number could not move whatever anyone wrote. Caught only because a routine `search_design` before starting surfaced that node. (3) RECOMMENDING THE ROLL-UP BE ADDED TO `seam_report`, which turned out to compare TWO LINKED DESIGNS and could not host it at all; the user chose that option on my description of it. Caught by reading the source before writing. || ⭐ THE COMMON MECHANISM, AND IT IS NOT LAZINESS: in all three the graph HELD THE ANSWER and the proposal was formed from the DETECTOR'S OUTPUT instead. A gap says what is absent; it cannot say whether the absence is a hole or a conclusion. `ifc:graph-export` had six unset axes and `ifc:mcp-tools-http` had one, reported IN IDENTICAL WORDS, and one of those absences was a hole while the other was a defended answer. ⇒ THE GUARD IS ONE CALL: `search_design` ON THE SUBJECT BEFORE PROPOSING A PLAN, NOT BEFORE WRITING THE NODE. By the time a node is being written the plan is already committed and the cost of abandoning it is paid in reputation as well as time. || ⚠️ AND THE SAME SESSION BROKE `rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` THREE TIMES, in scripts checking whether a tool call had worked: reading the JSON-RPC envelope for `result` rather than the tool result for `isError`. One of those silently reported five decisions as created when none was, and a later probe overwrote a real node with the word `probe`. ⇒ THAT RULE IS ONE OF THE THREE DOWNGRADED TO ADVISORY THE SAME DAY FOR HAVING NO DETECTOR — AND IT WAS BROKEN THREE TIMES BY THE AGENT WHO DOWNGRADED IT, WITHIN THE HOUR. The strongest argument yet that it is worth a detector: it is not an obscure rule, it is the one an agent breaks while working normally. || SOURCE: this session, 2026-08-23. Written from the conversation and the diffs, which is the only place the pattern exists — each instance is recorded separately, none of them together.
